newsitem.title: USA: Exxon denies market rumors, though gasoline firm.
newsitem.headline: Exxon denies market rumors, though gasoline firm.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Thursday that both its large refineries in the Gulf of Mexico were operating normally, denying market rumors that there was a fire or some other disruption.
Gasoline futures, nevertheless, rose sharply late in the day on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX).
"We are operating normally at both Baytown and Baton Rouge," said Exxon spokesman Bruce Thackett. "We've had a lot of calls on this...I don't know what its all about."
The Baton Rouge, Louisiana plant has a crude distillation capacity of 432,000 barrels a day (bpd) and Baytown, Texas refinery 411,000 bpd.
Traders said the rumors of a disruption might have sprung from talk, also unconfirmed, that Exxon was a large purchaser of gasoline in the Gulf of Mexico.
"There's talk they've been buying a lot more (than 100,000 gallons), across all ranges (grades)," said an East Coast products trader.
Gasoline futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) were up 1.10 cents to close at 62.84 cents a gallon on sympathy.

Some traders said that the futures move and the rumors didn't gel with their experience in the physical market. "We have barrels in the Gulf but we can't sell them. We went to Star Enterprises, the best bid in the market, and Exxon but they weren't buying," said a trader at a major commodities trading house.

"There is a lot of shenanigans going on the floor," he said, noting heavy buying of the May/June spread on futures in the last few days, giving some tradrs an interest in spreading rumors to lift the market. The May contract expires next Wednesday.
